audit.why: 51.62% over 370 games, EVEN at 6/10. The chart is honest about the shape: Camille takes level 1 and level 6, Singed takes the proxy stages and everything from first item on. The 'he may simply refuse to be in lane' framing is the correct read on why a favourable duel does not translate into a favourable lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is written as the stage where Camille's R turns off Singed's entire kit, with nothing said about what Singed gains at 6.
audit.why: Singed's level-6 ability is Insanity Potion, a 100s ult that among other things applies Grievous Wounds. Camille's Tactical Sweep self-heal is a real part of why she wins extended trades here, and it is halved the moment he drinks. Level 6 is still Camille's stage — the arena lock is worth more — but the spike is not one-sided, and a player told it is one-sided will commit into anti-heal and lose the trade.
audit.corrected: Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds stated in spikes[1].text, whys[4] and mid, with the sequencing cue to open before he drinks.

audit.whatIsWrong: Camille's passive is called 'your Passive shield' twice rather than Adaptive Defenses, Singed's Q is called 'his poison trail' rather than Poison Trail, his R is never named at all, and Camille's R is written without its article.
audit.why: Riot's names are Poison Trail (Q), Mega Adhesive (W), Fling (E), Insanity Potion (R) and Noxious Slipstream (P); Camille's are Adaptive Defenses and The Hextech Ultimatum. The two interactions that decide this lane are already half-present and now get numbers: Mega Adhesive grounds, which denies Hookshot outright, and Fling is only a 10s cooldown at rank 1 falling to 8s — shorter than Hookshot's 16s, so 'back off before his Fling is up' was quietly impossible advice as written.
audit.corrected: All abilities named; Fling's 10s and the fact it beats Hookshot's 16s stated; Mega Adhesive's grounding kept and tied to the E.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'back off before his Fling is up' and 'collapse when his Fling is down' both treat Fling as a long cooldown to wait out.
audit.why: Fling is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s. It is back before Hookshot is. The punishable cooldown in this matchup is Mega Adhesive at 17/16/15/14/13s, because that is the one that denies Camille's dash.
audit.corrected: Trade timing re-keyed to Fling's actual 10s and to Mega Adhesive as the cooldown that matters.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says when Camille should buy Grievous Wounds of her own.
audit.why: Singed's listed late build in this matchup's own text is Rylai's, Riftmaker and Liandry's — Riftmaker is the sustain item that makes him uncatchable, and it is exactly what anti-heal answers. The kit files do not carry item data, so I will not invent a timing.

edits.before: Once you have Q's empowered re-cast plus a point in W, you out-trade Singed before his poison trail out-ticks your Passive shield — E-stun in, slap the true-damage second hit, and back off before his Fling is up.
edits.after: Once you have Precision Protocol's re-cast plus a point in W you out-trade him before Poison Trail out-ticks Adaptive Defenses — E-stun in, land the true-damage second hit, and leave inside Fling's 10s.

edits.before: Hextech Ultimatum is the single tool that beats Singed's whole escape package — the arena cancels his raw move speed, his Fling-and-flee, and his Mega Adhesive, forcing the isolated 1v1 he spends the game avoiding.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum beats Singed's whole escape package — the arena cancels his move speed, Fling-and-flee and Mega Adhesive — but Insanity Potion halves your Tactical Sweep heal, so open before he drinks it.

edits.before: Hextech Ultimatum traps him in the arena, nullifying his move-speed escape, his Fling, and Mega Adhesive — the one window where his whole kite package is turned off.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum traps him with his move speed, Fling and Mega Adhesive all dead — but open before Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds halves your W heal.

edits.before: Your second point lands Q's true-damage re-cast plus a W slow — you out-trade his single-target poison trail before he can line up a Fling.
edits.after: Your second point lands Precision Protocol's true-damage re-cast plus a W slow — you out-trade Poison Trail before he lines up a 10s Fling.

edits.before: Land the E-stun into Q's true-damage second hit to win short trades before his poison trail out-ticks your Passive shield
edits.after: Land the E-stun into Precision Protocol's true-damage second hit before Poison Trail out-ticks your Adaptive Defenses shield

edits.before: Punish his proxy waves by collapsing while he is isolated and his Fling is on cooldown
edits.after: Punish his proxy waves by collapsing while he is isolated and Mega Adhesive's 17s is down

edits.before: Singed's early threat is his Fling — if he walks up, grabs you, and tosses you into his poison trail you eat a chunk and he strolls off untouched. Don't chase him through his own poison or facecheck for a free Q; instead farm with Q's empowered hit and wait for him to step up to last-hit, then E-stun in and re-cast Q for the true-damage second tick. His poison trail can't out-trade your Passive shield plus Q burst at this stage, but the instant you over-extend he Flings you into nothing and walks away.
edits.after: Singed's early threat is Fling — a 10s cooldown that grabs you, drops you in Poison Trail, and lets him stroll off untouched. Don't chase through his poison or facecheck for a free Q; farm with Precision Protocol's empowered hit, wait for him to step up to last-hit, then E-stun in and re-cast for the true-damage second tick. Poison Trail can't out-trade Adaptive Defenses plus that burst yet, but Mega Adhesive grounds your Hookshot, so never dash onto the puddle.

edits.before: This is your window. With a point in W for the max-HP outer-edge sweep and E off cooldown, you win every short trade — E-stun in, W the outer edge to slow and heal, double-tap Q before his poison stacks. At 6 your R answers his entire identity: it cancels his move-speed run-down, his Fling-and-flee, and his Mega Adhesive, locking him in a 1v1 where his speed is dead weight. The catch is he will try to proxy and avoid you entirely, so deny the proxy by holding the wave and collapsing only when he's isolated and his Fling is down.
edits.after: This is your window. With a point in W for the max-HP outer-edge sweep and E up, you win every short trade — E-stun in, W the outer edge to slow and heal, double-tap Q before Poison Trail stacks. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum answers his identity: move speed, Fling-and-flee and Mega Adhesive all dead inside the arena. Open before Insanity Potion, though — its Grievous Wounds halves your W heal. He will proxy to avoid all this, so hold the wave and collapse while Mega Adhesive's 17s is down.

notes: The original advice to 'back off before his Fling is up' was structurally impossible — Fling is 10s at rank 1 against Hookshot's 16s, so it is always back first. Retimed to Mega Adhesive, which is the cooldown that actually denies Camille's dash. Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds against Tactical Sweep's self-heal came from _missing-interactions.json and is supported by Riot's own antiHeal tag on the ability; it was completely absent from the matchup. I did not invent an anti-heal purchase timing for Camille — the kits carry no item data.
